title: Power Automate process mining: export object-centric models to a Microsoft Fabric semantic model
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documentation supports the optional export, licensing, OneLake control and its update API. The export control's path reaches the correct wizard step but could show the subsequent workspace selection more explicitly. The cited pages opened successfully despite the pre-check's rate-limit responses.

claims.claim: The model contains objects, including their ingested object attributes.

claims.claim: The model contains events and their ingested attributes.
claims.quote: Events | Entity holds list of all events in the process with reference to particular node in the Nodes table and ingested event level attributes as additional columns.

claims.claim: The model contains relationships between events and objects.
claims.quote: EventObjectRelations | Entity holds all relationships between Events and Objects “touched” by the execution of an event.

claims.claim: The model contains derived nodes used for visuals.
claims.quote: Nodes | Entity holds all nodes with reference to specific object and including the relevant calculated measures.

claims.claim: The model contains derived edges used for visuals.
claims.quote: Edges | Entity holds all edges identified between nodes with reference to particular object, nodes and including the relevant calculated measures.

claims.claim: Process executions are based on a leading object type.
claims.quote: Process execution data entities are calculated as process instances of interconnected objects based on a leading object type.

claims.claim: The model includes predefined relationships.
claims.quote: The published data model includes predefined relationships that handle filtering and interconnectivity of visuals.

claims.claim: Some relationships are hidden in the model.
claims.quote: Some relationships are hidden in the model.

claims.claim: Only one relationship between the same two tables can be active.
claims.quote: This limitation exists because only one relationship between the same two tables can be active in semantic models.

claims.claim: Lakehouse column sanitisation allows English letters, digits and underscores.
claims.quote: Allowed characters include: a-z: lowercase English letters; A-Z: uppercase English letters; 0-9: digits; _: underscore

claims.claim: Other characters are replaced by underscores in Lakehouse delta-table column names.
claims.quote: All other characters are replaced with an underscore (_) as part of the sanitization process.

claims.claim: Semantic-model columns retain their original column names.
claims.quote: Lakehouse delta table columns therefore use the sanitized column names, whereas semantic model columns use the original column names.

claims.claim: Export can be interrupted when sanitisation produces identical names, such as Customer_Name and Customer Name.
claims.quote: This process might result in rare situations where export isn't successful, as the ingested data source includes two columns that result in identical names after sanitization—Customer_Name and Customer Name.

claims.claim: The user is notified with a specific error message when this naming collision interrupts export.
claims.quote: The export is interrupted and user is notified with the specific error message.
